Embedding dimensions refer to the number of features or parameters that need to be learned during training an embedding model. In natural language processing (NLP) and machine translation tasks, embeddings are used to convert text into numerical vectors that can be processed by neural networks.

The dimensionality of an embedding is typically defined as the number of unique words in a vocabulary. For example, if you have 10,000 unique words in your vocabulary, then the dimensionality of the embedding would be 10,000.

However, it's important to note that the exact dimensionality can vary depending on the specific task and the size of the dataset being used for training.
